name: mkldnn_adaptive_avg_pool2d
description: Representative ATen signature, copied verbatim and NOT an exclusive ABI: aten::mkldnn_adaptive_avg_pool2d(Tensor self, int[2] output_size) -> Tensor. The original Gems pytest owns the full contract: it defines the overloads, keyword arguments, returns, error behavior, aliasing and mutation support, so tests must not be narrowed to this one representative signature and the reference behavior must not be adapted to fit it. All supplied registered schemas, verbatim: aten::mkldnn_adaptive_avg_pool2d.out(Tensor self, int[2] output_size, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!) ; aten::mkldnn_adaptive_avg_pool2d(Tensor self, int[2] output_size) -> Tensor. Semantics derived from the tests: adaptive average pooling over the two spatial extents of a 4-D mkldnn-layout operand self of shape (N, C, H, W), producing the requested output_size (H_out, W_out) supplied as a two-element Python list; every extent of output_size must be positive and divide the corresponding spatial extent, and non-4-D inputs or zero, negative or non-divisible output_size raise RuntimeError. The returned tensor keeps the mkldnn layout (torch._mkldnn) and the operand device, and its dense values match the ATen reference for contiguous inputs, non-contiguous host views, empty (zero-extent) operands and special-value inputs. Dtype coverage includes float32, bfloat16, float16, int8 and uint8; the operator is host-only because the operand must carry the mkldnn layout and the conversion has no accelerator path. The other registered overload is keyword-only out: it requires an existing mkldnn buffer, writes it in place and returns that same object, so this representative default overload mutates nothing and aliases nothing while the out overload mutates and returns its out parameter; those conditional, overload-dependent effects remain expressed by the original pytest rather than by this single-overload model.
